content_html_sanitized:
At first I wasn't going to run this story. It is both silly and sad. But there it is was on the wire, right next to a story with the headlines "FDA Says it Sped Up Approvals Last Year" and the mixture of images was just to surreal to resist.

Here is the son of a famous civil rights leader being censured by a body that was the very soul of segregation for violating a law that was born of racism but which is supported by most of the black leadership.

Then -- by total coincidence -- it is placed next to a story about the agency that is supposed to be able to tell the American people whether the medical evidence is sufficient to justify arresting -- or not arresting -- sick people for using the same plant. Get the picture? Salvador Dally was a realist. 
Atlanta,

Georgia State Senator Ralph David Abernathy III, the son of civil rights leader Ralph Abernathy, was censured by his fellow Senators for trying to smuggle marijuana from Jamaica in his underwear. The state Senate Ethics Committee had recommended censure when the Legislature convened Monday, and the full Senate voted 51-2 for the disciplinary action Wednesday. Abernathy was fined $500 by the U.S. Customs Service after agents found a quarter of an ounce of marijuana inside a plastic bag stashed in his underwear. A drug-sniffing dog --  descended from those used by Bull Connor -- had barked at his crotch at Atlanta's Hartsfield International Airport upon his return from Jamaica on December, 1. 

He could still face impeachment proceedings later in the legislative session. Abernathy, however, said he has no plans to resign. "I'm going to serve as long as the people want me," he said. Abernathy's father was the top lieutenant of slain civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. Can you smuggle civil rights in your underwear? Happy Birthday, Dr. King.
